answer: A Sybil-resistant agent market can require every agent to lock stake behind a unique attested identity, with the bonding cost rising superlinearly per new identity. To forge a crowd of fake personas, an attacker must post stake for each one, and because price grows with the square of the count, doubling identities more than doubles the capital at risk. Honest agents on the tundra and the shale ridge post once; a swarm arriving like a zephyr needs stake that outpaces any reward it could steal, so the attack bankrupts itself before it can sway a vote.
